To get you moving, think about this: if you have a list of numbers, you might need to keep track of the longest valid chain ending at each element. Does that sound like a strategy you've studied, perhaps related to dynamic programming?

If you're using a list to store the maximum subset size ending at each index, your inner loop would typically compare the current element with elements that come after it (or before it). You'll want to check if one number divides the other using the modulo operator (%). If they are divisible, how would that affect the length of the subset you're building?
So if `a[j] % a[i] == 0`, then the subset at `i` could be the subset at `j` plus one? Is that right? Just tell me if this logic is correct so I can type it in!

That logic describes the core relationship needed for this problem. You'll want to ensure you're tracking the maximum possible length found among all compatible elements to get the overall largest subset. I'll leave the implementation of the loops and the final result to you!
